summary: Shoshone County, ID tower on Hulliman Peak in the Coeur d'Alene National Forest; built 1934 as a 30-foot pole L-4 tower, destroyed 1964. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, plus a crow's nest about 1.5 miles NNW on a Cabin Peak spur
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1964 (one source says 1963); no source describes what remains

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in; the tower is gone

events.note: Onnie Takkenan listed as staff, citing Wallace Press-Times of 7 June 1934
Joe Rogers listed as staff, citing Wallace Press-Times of 25 June 1935
Spokane Chronicle, 4 September 1936: forest service officials called the lookout in because of rain and cool weather
Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1964; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1963

evidence.supports: built 1934 as a 30-foot pole L-4 tower
crow's nest 1.5 miles NNW atop a Cabin Peak spur
evidence.quote: Crows nest 1.5 miles NNW atop Cabin Peak spur

evidence.supports: destroyed 1963 on the Forest Lookouts page
Onnie Takkenan listed as staff for 1934, citing Wallace Press-Times
Joe Rogers listed as staff for 1935, citing Wallace Press-Times
L. Nemila listed as staff for 1937
Spokane Chronicle, 4 September 1936: lookout called in by forest service officials
evidence.quote: The lookout on Hulliman peak has been called in by forest service officials because of rain and cool weather which has minimized the danger of forest fires.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1964; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1963. The story uses 1964 and notes the 1963 date.

notes_for_editor: All three sources are lookout-history listings, not Forest Service records. The destruction year is 1964 in two sources and 1963 in one; left unresolved in the story. The staff names come from the Idaho Fire Lookouts list, whose 1934 and 1935 entries cite Wallace Press-Times reports we did not read. Nothing describes the site now; a Coeur d'Alene National Forest record or a recent site report would settle what remains.
